parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the features of the case study method.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Design an alternative way to investigate activation of the right hippocampus as a case study
and describe how it could be conducted.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Evaluate this alternative way of studying activation of the right hippocampus in methodological
and practical terms.

text: Maguire et al. (taxi drivers) carried out an experiment which studied activation of the right
hippocampus. An alternative way to investigate this would be to use the case study method.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline what is meant by the ‘situational explanation of behaviour’ in psychology.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one finding from the Haney, Banks and Zimbardo study that supports the situational
explanation of behaviour.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Discuss the strengths and weaknesses of investigating the situational explanation of
behaviour using the Haney, Banks and Zimbardo study as an example.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss the extent to which the Haney, Banks and Zimbardo study was ethical. 
Section B (20 marks)
Answer one question in this section.

text: Haney, Banks and Zimbardo conducted a study to investigate social roles in a mock prison.

parts.text:

Rosenhan (sane in insane places)
Thigpen and Cleckley (multiple personality disorder)
Dement and Kleitman (sleep and dreaming)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how qualitative data were collected in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: What are the strengths of collecting qualitative data?

parts.label: (b)
